notes: The pose reader is a better model, and every joint can be fixed by hand. The first live extraction read a woman lying on her stomach with her feet up behind her, and MediaPipe drew her legs running down and away from her body: it guesses hidden and foreshortened limbs from a standing prior, and its confidence score says whether a joint is in frame, not whether the guess is right, so the bad legs passed the filter. Painting with that skeleton would have held the GPU to a pose that does not exist. The pod now runs RTMW, the whole-body model of the DWPose line, trained on artwork as well as photographs and far steadier on lying, turned and partly hidden bodies; MediaPipe stays as the fallback if the model download fails, and the log says which one answered. Both now hand back the same thing, eighteen joints in the OpenPose order, which is what is stored from here on; poses read earlier are converted as they are used. And because no reader gets every joint right on the pictures this library is for, tapping a pose's picture opens an editor: drag any joint where it belongs, tap its name to switch it off so the ControlNet leaves that part of the body to the prompt, mirror left and right when the reader swapped them, and Reset to go back to what the reader saw. Changes save as you go. Thumbnails are kept a little larger to make the editing comfortable.
